keywords: why ai videos look the same
title: AI video template look: why "make me a cool video" fails
description: Asking AI for "a cool video" leaves every choice blank, so it fills the font, colours, text motion, pacing and ending with its defaults. That's why AI videos look the same. The Video Brief shows how to close those blanks with one written brief. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: "Make me a cool video" gets a template. A quote card from The Video Brief, section 06: "Leave a blank, and AI fills it with its default." A second card lists the blanks: the font, the colours, how text appears, the pacing, the ending. Bottom line: A better tool won't fix it. Fewer blanks will. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: AI video prompt tip: write a never-list before you prompt
description: A never-list tells AI what your video must never do: no drop shadows, glows or bouncing text, nothing that flashes for one frame. Without one, AI places elements wherever there is space. The Video Brief includes the full brief template with the never-list. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Write a never-list before you prompt. A dark copy block: Never: no drop shadows, glows or bouncing text; nothing that appears in a single frame; "link in bio" never as plain text. A quote card from section 07 about AI placing elements on top of a character's hand. Bottom line: The never-list does the most work: it's where your taste goes. Mint footer with The Video Brief and theexactmethod.com.

title: Edit AI video with Claude: feedback that gets a fix, not a guess
description: "Make it better" gets a guess. A precise note gets a fix: the timestamp, what is wrong, and what to do instead, all in one message. The Video Brief has the fix-message pattern plus the checks to run on every render. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: Feedback that gets a fix, not a guess. Three cards: Vague, "Make it better." crossed out; Precise, "0:22: the card covers the presenter's hand. Move the cards up so the hand is clear."; The pattern, timestamp, what is wrong, what to do instead. Bottom line: All notes in one message, fixed in one pass. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: Check AI video with the sound off: 3 checks before you post
description: Watch your AI-made video on your phone with the sound off. Does the hook work, does every caption land on its word, is the small text readable? These are 3 of the 8 checks in The Video Brief. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Watch your AI video with the sound off. Three cards: The first three seconds, the hook works with the sound off; Timing, every caption and card lands on its word, not after it; Readability, small text that is fine on a laptop and unreadable on a phone. Bottom line: 3 of the 8 checks in the guide. Watch it on your phone. Mint footer with The Video Brief and theexactmethod.com.

title: ElevenLabs commercial use: the free plan has no license
description: If your videos promote anything you sell, that is commercial use, and ElevenLabs says its free plan cannot be used for any commercial purpose. The Starter plan was $6 a month in November 2026, license included. The Video Brief covers the voice setup and cost. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: ElevenLabs free plan? Not for videos that sell. A quote card from the ElevenLabs help center: "The free plan does not include a commercial license and cannot be used for any commercial purpose." Two cards: Commercial use, videos that promote anything you sell; Starter plan, Nov 2026, $6 a month, commercial license included. Bottom line: Check the license before you post. Mint footer with The Video Brief.
source: ElevenLabs pricing page and help center, checked Nov 2026 (cited in The Video Brief)

title: ElevenLabs API key for Claude: restrict it so it can't overspend
description: Before you hand Claude an ElevenLabs API key, restrict it: a credit limit below your plan, and only Text to Speech, Voices and Models turned on. The Video Brief walks through the full key setup and the prompt that hands it to Claude. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Give Claude a voice key that can't overspend. Three cards: Restrict Key, on, with a credit limit below your plan's total; Endpoints, Text to Speech: Access, Voices: Read, Models: Access; Everything else, No Access. Bottom line: A restricted key only does what you allow. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: AI storyboard prompt: plan every shot before AI builds the video
description: Ask Claude for a storyboard before it builds anything: one row per shot, timed to the real voice files, with what is on screen and why each shot is there. A shot that can't say why it's there is usually filler. The Video Brief has the full prompt. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: Get a storyboard before AI builds anything. A mint-edged copy block with the prompt: Before building anything, write a storyboard: one row per shot, with start and end times taken from the real lengths of the voice files; what's on screen and how it enters and leaves; and one sentence per shot on why it is there at that moment. Bottom line: A shot that can't say why it's there is usually filler.

title: AI video captions late? Time them to the real voice files
description: When captions drift, the fix is a timing rule in your brief: time everything to the real voice files, never to an estimate, and save the word timings with every voice file. Half a second late is enough to feel wrong. More in The Video Brief. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Captions late? Time them to the voice. A dark copy block: Time everything to the real voice files, never to an estimate. A quote card from section 07: "Without a timing rule, captions drift. Half a second late is enough to feel wrong." Bottom line: Save the word timings with every voice file. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: Reels export settings for AI video: the one line your brief needs
description: Add one export line to every AI video brief: 1080x1920, 30 fps, voice at about -14 LUFS, peaks under -1 dB. Without it, a video can go out small and quieter than everything around it in the feed. The Video Brief has the full brief template. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: One export line every AI video needs. A copy block: Export. 1080x1920, 30 fps, voice at about -14 LUFS, peaks under -1 dB. A quote card from section 07: "Without an export block, a video can go out at 720x1280 with the voice at -20 LUFS, quieter than everything around it in the feed." Bottom line: Check every render: size, frame rate, loudness. Mint footer with The Video Brief.

title: Claude Code skills: read one before you install it
description: A skill is someone else's instructions, and often someone else's code. This prompt has Claude read the README and SKILL.md first and flag anything unsafe or anything that needs an API key. The Video Brief lists the skills for AI video and their licenses. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Read a Claude skill before you install it. A dark copy block with the prompt: Before you install anything, read its README and SKILL.md and tell me in one line whether anything looks unsafe or needs an API key. Install only the parts I name. Bottom line: A skill is someone else's code. Check the license too. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: Make Reels with Claude: no editing app, just a brief
description: With Claude Code, Claude builds the video in code, renders it, checks it and sends you the file. You set it up once, then every video starts from a script, voice files and one written brief. The Video Brief walks you through the whole workflow. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Make Reels with no editing app. A quote card from The Video Brief, section 01: "Claude builds the video in code, renders it, checks it and sends you the file. You never open an editing app." Two cards: Once, the setup; Every video, a script, voice files and one written brief. Bottom line: Your job: describe it precisely and judge the result. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: Claude video prompt: check stills before the full render
description: A full render takes minutes, while a still shows most problems in seconds. This prompt has Claude render the busiest moments as stills and check them against your never-list before rendering the whole video. The Video Brief has the full build prompt. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: Check stills before the full render. A mint-edged copy block: Before the full render, render stills of the three busiest moments and check them against the never-list. Fix anything that fails, then render the full video. Bottom line: A full render takes minutes. A still shows most problems in seconds. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

description: Making AI Reels in code needs Claude with Claude Code and an ElevenLabs account; Claude installs Remotion and ffmpeg itself. Remotion is free for individuals and small teams. Prices as of November 2026 are in The Video Brief, with the full setup. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Make AI Reels with just two accounts. title: AI video brand colors: give AI your hex codes and fonts
description: Leave the colours blank and AI picks its default. The look block in the brief names every colour as a hex code (background, text, accent, mistakes) and every font by name, so the video matches your brand. The Video Brief has the full template. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Dark green pin. Headline: Give AI your colours as hex codes. A copy block, the look block: Colours as hex codes: background, text, accent, mistakes. Fonts, by name: headlines, body. A quote card from section 06: "Leave a blank, and AI fills it with its default." Bottom line: Name every colour, or AI picks one for you. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.

title: Claude video prompt: make AI ask before it builds anything
description: Add one line to your video prompt so Claude asks about anything unclear in your brief instead of guessing, and builds nothing until you approve the storyboard. A question costs seconds; a wrong render costs minutes. More in The Video Brief. Free PDF at theexactmethod.com.
alt_text: Light paper pin. Headline: Make AI ask before it builds your video. A dark copy block: If anything in the brief is unclear, ask instead of guessing. Don't build anything until I approve the storyboard. Bottom line: A question costs seconds. A wrong render costs minutes. Mint footer: Free PDF: The Video Brief, theexactmethod.com.
